name: The Strokes
label: Rough Trade
lede: Rough Trade heard ten seconds of a $600 demo down a phone line and signed it. Twenty-five years on, the five New Yorkers on that tape are still the only lineup the Strokes have had.

hero.by: Photo: Roger Woolman, March 2002. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Five friends, one basement, $600
eras.text: Julian Casablancas, Nick Valensi and Fabrizio Moretti met at Dwight School in Manhattan, Nikolai Fraiture came from Casablancas's childhood, and Albert Hammond Jr. turned up last. They rehearsed for a year before playing a note in public, then spent another hustling the Lower East Side until one demo crossed the Atlantic.

years.h: Hammond moves to New York and into Casablancas's flat
years.p: Albert Hammond Jr. knew Julian Casablancas from Institut Le Rosey, the Swiss boarding school. Two weeks after they ran into each other in Manhattan they were roommates, and he was the band's fifth member.
years.xp:
Casablancas, Valensi and Moretti had been playing together since 1997, and Fraiture was a friend from the Lycée Français. Hammond, by his own account, looked the part but "still needed guitar lessons."

Casablancas wrote the songs and taught them chord by chord. "It's D to G. Yeah, kinda like that, but you're holding the chord wrong," is how Hammond remembers The Modern Age arriving.

years.h: First show as the Strokes, at the Spiral, for six people
years.p: The plan had been a year of rehearsal first, mostly at the Music Building in Midtown. Before the gig they went to see the Eddie Murphy film Bowfinger to calm their nerves.
years.xp:
"It's hilarious that we were so nervous playing to six people, all of whom we knew," Hammond told the Guardian. He thinks the show was "probably terrible."

After that came HiFi Bar, the Luna Lounge and the Mercury Lounge, where a young booker named Ryan Gentles would soon quit his job to manage them.

years.h: Snowed in at the Luna Lounge, they debut The Modern Age and Last Nite
years.p: Stuck in the middle slot after an argument over set times, the band played the two new songs for the first time and kicked over the drum kit. Their friends walked out with them, leaving the headliner an empty room.

years.src: The Guardian · Wikipedia: Is This It
years.h: Gordon Raphael cuts the demo: three days, $600, a basement
years.p: Raphael thought the Strokes looked "a bit too stylish" when he saw them, but handed them his card. The basement session produced The Modern Age, Last Nite and Barely Legal.
years.xp:
Raphael had gone to the free show for the opening band, Come On. "The Strokes called me back. I never heard from Come On," he told the Guardian. In his basement, he said, they sounded far more interesting than on stage.

This was the year the New York Times ran a cover with an electric guitar drawn as a gravestone.

years.cap: The Strokes on a New York club stage, c. 2000
years.h: Ten seconds over a transatlantic phone line win over Rough Trade
years.p: Matt Hickey, a Mercury Lounge booker scouting for [[Rough Trade|4f4b0013-1704-4936-a769-e6e8a6e08ff8]], called [[Geoff Travis|70437714-3183-4916-947f-e5ba2154d16a]] in London at about 7am and held the phone up to The Modern Age. Gentles had already booked the band for four December nights at the club.
years.xp:
"Matt phoned up at about seven o'clock in the morning and played about ten seconds of the EP over the phone, and that was it," Travis recalled in Lizzy Goodman's Meet Me in the Bathroom. "That was the moment."

Rough Trade had only just been relaunched. Within a year it had signed the Strokes, [[British Sea Power|8830afec-83b3-4213-aad0-f6377f1d73ac]] and [[The Libertines|82b304c0-7da4-45d3-896a-0767c7ae1141]].

eras.title: Everybody in London wants a Stroke
eras.text: A demo became a Rough Trade EP, the EP became NME's single of the week, and by spring the band were at the center of the biggest bidding war for a rock band in years. Is This It came out in a world that changed in New York two weeks after the UK release.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Modern Age · Louder · The Guardian
years.h: Rough Trade releases the demo as The Modern Age EP
years.p: Raphael's basement tape goes out as is. NME makes it single of the week, gives away Last Nite as a free MP3, and the EP goes on to sell 30,000 copies.

years.h: The first UK shows sell out on the strength of three songs
years.p: Rough Trade flew the band over the month the EP came out. A sold-out UK tour followed, then US support slots for Doves and [[Guided by Voices|6c85f4c3-026c-4c16-9a7c-f546f42ed0fb]].

years.cap: The Strokes at the Troubadour, Los Angeles, 2001
years.src: Wikipedia: Is This It · Wikipedia: The Modern Age
years.h: RCA wins the bidding war; Rough Trade keeps Britain
years.p: After the most heated chase for a rock band in years, the Strokes sign to RCA for most of the world. Gentles quits the Mercury Lounge to manage them full-time.

years.big: "Imagine you took a time machine into the future."
years.src: The Guardian · Wikipedia: Is This It
years.h: Casablancas storms out on Raphael, then calls him back
years.p: Rough Trade wanted [[Gil Norton|2270fb9d-0f39-4f6f-aba9-ef2bee2f3755]], producer of [[Pixies|b6b2bb8d-54a9-491f-9607-7b546023b433]], to make the album. The band found the Norton sessions "too clean" and scrapped them, and Casablancas called Raphael with that line as the brief.
years.xp:
Over dinner Casablancas told Raphael he could make the record if he'd say he was a better producer than Norton. Raphael wouldn't. "So he stood up and said: 'Fuck you. Now we have to use Gil Norton,'" Raphael told the Guardian. A few weeks later the phone rang.

The record took six weeks at Transporterraum, with Casablancas singing through a small Peavey practice amp and the drums caught by three microphones. RCA's A&R man initially found it unprofessional; Casablancas won him over by playing the new songs on a boom box.

years.h: Moretti breaks his hand after the Glasgow show
years.p: A fall puts the drummer in hospital mid-tour. Two of the last five UK dates are cancelled and family friend Matt Romano flies over to fill in.

years.src: Wikipedia: Is This It · Wikipedia: The Strokes
yt: Last Nite (official video, dir. Roman Coppola)
years.h: Is This It lands in Australia first, Britain via Rough Trade on August 27
years.p: Eleven songs, mostly first takes, mixed as they went. The UK release lines up with Reading and Leeds, where the band get bumped up the bill twice, from a tent to the main stage.
years.xp:
The international cover is Colin Lane's photo of his then-girlfriend's hip and a leather-gloved hand. HMV and Woolworths objected and stocked it anyway. For America, Casablancas swapped it for particle tracks in a bubble chamber: he phoned Gentles to say he'd found "something even cooler than the ass picture."

The title has no question mark because, the band said, it did not look right. Reviews ran from Pitchfork's 9.1 to a perfect 10 in NME, and the album was named best of 2001 by NME, Time, Entertainment Weekly and Billboard.

years.h: After September 11, New York City Cops comes off the US album
years.p: RCA pushes the American CD back two weeks and Casablancas writes When It Started to replace the song. The US vinyl, released on September 11, still has it.

eras.title: Band of the year, then the second record
eras.text: The Strokes spent 2002 collecting awards on both sides of the Atlantic and opening for the Rolling Stones. Following up a debut that critics were already ranking against the Velvet Underground took two producers and two years.

years.h: Saturday Night Live gives Is This It a 60 percent bump
years.p: The album had been moving 20,000 copies a week in the US. After the SNL slot it climbs from number 63 to its peak of 33, and goes gold in February.

years.cap: At Levi's Anti-VMA party, New York, August 30, 2002
years.h: [[Jack White|3ae2fb37-8a23-429d-9920-bac811c4fc22]] plays the solo on New York City Cops at Radio City
years.p: After headlining the Carling Weekend for a second straight summer, the Strokes share a Radio City Music Hall bill with [[The White Stripes|11ae9fbb-f3d7-4a47-936f-4c0a04d3b3b5]].

years.h: Godrich out, Raphael back: Room on Fire
years.p: Sessions with Radiohead producer [[Nigel Godrich|52de022d-5401-427f-8301-ff1b8be11a7a]] were shelved and never released. The album goes gold and gets the band a Spin cover each and a first Rolling Stone cover. Valensi plays the keyboard-like part on 12:51 on guitar.

years.h: Kings of Leon and Regina Spektor open the Room on Fire tour
years.p: Spektor and the band cut Modern Girls & Old Fashion Men together on the road; it became the B-side of Reptilia.

eras.title: A number one, then a long nap
eras.text: First Impressions of Earth gave the Strokes their first UK number one and their roughest reviews. After a long 2006 on the road the band stopped, and for nearly four years the members worked on their own records.

years.h: David Kahne replaces Raphael for First Impressions of Earth
years.p: Juicebox leaked in September and was rushed out early. The album went to number one in the UK, number four in the US, two weeks as iTunes' most downloaded album. Reviews were mixed. Fraiture called it "like a scientific breakthrough."

years.h: The longest US tour yet, after 18 sold-out UK shows
years.p: NME names them Best International Band in February. The year runs through Roskilde, Fuji Rock and five dates opening for Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers.

years.h: Casablancas tells a crowd the band is taking a break
years.p: An email from Gentles soon confirms the "much needed break." Hammond, Casablancas, Fraiture and Moretti go off to make records of their own.

years.h: The Strokes play Dingwalls as Venison, for 487 people
years.p: Their first show since October 2006, under a fake name in a small Camden room. No new songs.

years.h: Back as a headliner, from Lollapalooza to Austin City Limits
years.p: The comeback summer took in Isle of Wight, Lollapalooza, Roskilde and Outside Lands before ending in Austin, with the fourth album still unfinished.

eras.title: Five writers, one inbox
eras.text: Angles was the first Strokes record written by all five, and the strain showed in the interviews. After Comedown Machine the RCA contract ran out, the band moved to Casablancas's own label, and live shows became rare events.

q: I won't do the next album if we make it like this.
years.h: Written together, sung apart: the making of Angles
years.p: Sessions with [[Joe Chiccarelli|2a250f44-5473-4dc9-a8ba-2320fb31b2f9]] yielded one keeper, Life Is Simple in the Moonlight. The rest was rebuilt with engineer Gus Oberg at Hammond's home studio in Port Jervis, with Casablancas recording his vocals on his own.
years.xp:
Valensi told the press he wouldn't make another record that way: "Working in a fractured way, not having a singer there." Casablancas's ideas often arrived by email. He told Pitchfork, "it took me being a little mute to force the initiative."

Casablancas later said the songs were all written in a room together and only the vocals were done separately. Wikipedia also reports that Hammond missed early sessions while in rehab for drug use. The album went to number four in the US and number one in Australia.

years.h: Elvis Costello joins them at Madison Square Garden
years.p: The live Taken for a Fool from that night became the B-side of the studio single. That spring the band also headlined Coachella.

years.h: Comedown Machine arrives with no interviews, no TV and no tour
years.p: A Reddit user found the cover hidden on the band's website in January. The album was the last on their RCA contract.

years.h: Future Present Past EP comes out on Casablancas's Cult Records
years.p: Three new songs and a Moretti remix of Oblivius, released to coincide with their Governors Ball headline set. Cult also signs the band to its roster.

years.h: Fraiture calls Lollapalooza Argentina their biggest show ever
years.p: The crowd was reported at 90,000. The same year Lizzy Goodman's oral history Meet Me in the Bathroom, named after a Room on Fire song, made the Strokes its center.

years.h: Albert Hammond Sr. says the Strokes are working with [[Rick Rubin|07aebfa0-55d6-47e0-a284-12330e3eae0d]]
years.p: His son corrected him on Twitter: they had met Rubin and played him some ideas, but "we are not in the studio recording."

eras.title: The Grammy and the comeback
eras.text: A rough 2019 comeback tour led to The New Abnormal, made with Rick Rubin and released as the world locked down. It won a Grammy. The seventh album, cut in Costa Rica, arrived in 2026 with one Stroke missing from the stage.

years.h: The Adults Are Talking opens the comeback tour
years.p: The band debuted the song at a Los Angeles benefit, their first show in two years. The tour that followed had sound trouble at All Points East, storms at Governors Ball and a festival in Spain cancelled outright.

years.cap: Casablancas at the Roundhouse, London, February 19, 2020
years.h: They name the album at a Bernie Sanders rally
years.p: Casablancas announced The New Abnormal and its April 10 release date from the stage at the University of New Hampshire.

years.h: The New Abnormal, produced by Rick Rubin
years.p: The first Strokes album in seven years, out through Cult and RCA. Critics called it a return to form, and in March 2021 it won Best Rock Album at the Grammys.

years.cap: Casablancas and Hammond at Tempelhof, Berlin, June 12, 2022
years.h: Opening stadiums for the [[Red Hot Chili Peppers|8bfac288-ccc5-448d-9573-c33ea2aa5c30]]
years.p: In October, Rubin says he has been recording a new Strokes album with them in Costa Rica.

years.h: Oblivius closes Coachella under a montage condemning US interventions
years.p: The video named CIA-backed coups and the wars in Gaza and Iran. Pitchfork, Variety and the Guardian all covered it.

years.h: Valensi sits out the tour; Steve Schiltz of Longwave fills in
years.p: The band gave no reason. Schiltz has known them since the early days of the New York scene. Valensi was also absent from the Going Shopping video.

years.h: Reality Awaits, a month late
years.p: Pushed back from June 26 so streaming would line up with the vinyl, as Hammond explained in a tweet he quickly deleted. Some reviews took issue with Casablancas's heavy use of vocoder.
years.xp: The same day the band posted In Transit: Part II, a 10-minute film of the Costa Rica sessions with Rubin and a sequel to their original tour documentary.

sources.title: The Guardian: The Strokes, how we made Is This It (Dave Simpson, 2015)
Louder: How The Strokes saved rock'n'roll with a demo (Niall Doherty, via Yahoo)
